title: Repin the Cyclotron engine and web package to their releases
description:
Pin the Python extra to Cyclotron main b2234be (the ui-v0.2.1 tag's commit) and the web package to the ui-v0.2.1 release tarball, then remove the References tab's browser-only rendering of the review control: ui-v0.2.1 derives the control's field ids from the item and decision, so server and client renders agree.

Done when: pyproject and poetry.lock pin b2234be; package.json and the lockfile pin cyclotron-0.2.1.tgz; ReferenceRelevanceReview renders on the server; the References tab scenarios pass with no hydration error.

## Current next-step plan — 2026-10-17

Verified 2026-10-17: Cyclotron PR25 https://github.com/AnthusAI/Cyclotron/pull/25 merged into develop at323d0b587d9057e0e93b99df2383bde70b2edc91, head61323ae0840fb3a787439c09d7a08674ff677aed. Test and diagrams checks SUCCESS; release SKIPPED. Source prepares UI0.2.2, but remote UI tags stop atui-v0.2.1 (peeledb2234be79d83231a4ed69f17a928b5049ab364a4); no ui-v0.2.2 tag. Latest published engine releasev0.20.1 (c09f70b33b2b96a4e4cc2acca360af47d26620a8, published2026-10-12). PR25 is not an ancestor of current main. Merged develop source is not a published dependency or production proof.

The original ui-v0.2.1 pin acceptance is a historical checkpoint and does not cover PrimingPanel. Next: publish the reviewed shared engine/UI artifacts through the existing release workflow after owner-authorized main promotion; verify tag commit and downloadable package contents; then update Papyrus/Cyclotron consumer declarations and lockfiles to those exact published versions. Fresh install/build/SSR/shared exports and both-mode priming acceptance must pass. No moving branch or unpublished0.2.2 URL may be described as a released pin. Package publication and consumer pinning are separate receipts; no release or main merge is authorized by this documentation update.

Authority: Ryan requested this plan as the permanent Kanbus record. This action updates documentation only. The desired product outcomes are requested priorities, not claims of implementation or hosted acceptance. Existing implementation owners retain their approvals; recommendations needing further scope, release, permission or migration direction stay explicitly gated. No feature code, deployment, paid call, permission change or unrelated merge is performed here.
